verdict.rationale: Ramp's own agents run continuously in the background, coding expenses, flagging fraud, auto-approving in-policy spend and escalating the rest. Users configure rules-based workflows, auto-lock and auto-rebook behaviors, and per-agent keys with long-running access "for background agents that run on a schedule." The CLI (non-interactive mode, client-credentials agent login) and webhooks are documented for scripted, scheduled and event-triggered automation. Missing for 10: a first-party scheduler or automation builder (scheduling relies on the user's own cron/CI), detail on how users author custom autonomous automations beyond policy and workflow rules, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
